meta.title: Research Overview
meta.subtitle: $\pi$ shift Bragg grating cavities for acousto optic sensing
meta.author: Evyatar Rubin

frames.title: Main conclusions
items: Changing the teeth trades loss against mode width; the cavity and lateral structures do not.
TM radiates in the propagation plane: a trench or a SiN post row \textcolor{green!50!black}{reduces its loss}; TE does not.
Inverse design at fixed width \textcolor{green!50!black}{beats every hand tuned lever}, still below the lab's overshoot.
Reflectors, scatterers and in core structures \textcolor{red!75!black}{do not help}.

frames.title: Every lever reduces loss; only a few leave the mode width unchanged
Reflectors, scatterers and in core structures do not help
$Q$ at a 20\,$\mu$m mode and a −3\,dB peak
frames.caption: Each device lengthened until its peak is −3\,dB at a 20\,$\mu$m mode. Lateral structures give about a third more $Q$, inverse design about 6×; the TE overshoot bar is projected.

frames.heading: Details
frames.subheading: TE, TE versus TM, TM levers, inverse design

frames.title: TE: apodization reduces loss and widens the mode
items: Linear apodization: loss reduced, mode much wider. Tanh: the same gain with less widening.
A few apodized periods are enough; more add nothing.
The lab's overshoot apodization is far stronger, and only its amplitude sets the mode width.

frames.title: TE: shifting the innermost teeth recycles the leak
items: Shifting the innermost teeth outward reduces loss with the mode width unchanged.
Light that would leak at the cavity is redirected into the mode; the far field collapses to one lobe.
A two tooth particle swarm design gave the best transmission per width; fabricated devices confirmed the shift range.

frames.title: TE versus TM
items: Same length: TM couples more weakly, so lower loss, lower $Q$, wider mode.
Same peak transmission: TM is longer and its $Q$ is about three times higher.
At the operating point the plain gratings tie. TM radiates in the propagation plane, TE upward.

frames.title: TM: the teeth behave as in TE, but the shift works differently
items: Apodization reduces loss, widens the mode, and saturates.
A large shift of the innermost teeth widens the mode and shows no optimum; TM does not recycle at the cavity.
Once apodization saturates, small shifts on many teeth \textcolor{green!50!black}{add further gain at fixed width}; the inverse design uses this.

frames.title: TM: a trench reduces loss, a third more $Q$ at the benchmark
frames.caption: The trench returns the in plane radiation by total internal reflection; the mode width is unchanged. A trench stopping at the core top keeps most of the gain in one lithography step.

frames.title: TM: a row of SiN posts does the same, one lithography step
items: The row is a weak grating: its period sets the beam angle, $n_\text{clad}\,\sin\theta = n_\text{eff} - \lambda/\Lambda$.
Aimed at the radiation lobe, sliding the row sets the phase: one phase cancels the lobe, the opposite grows it.
A second row on the other side adds a few percent; a third adds nothing.

frames.title: Inverse design: what is optimized
items: 3D adjoint optimization of the 25 innermost teeth per side (depth, width, shift), the cavity width and the post row, TM.
Objective: peak transmission. Constraints: the mode width and the resonance wavelength are held fixed.
Width penalties and second moment proxies failed; projecting each gradient step onto both constraints works.

frames.title: Inverse design: what it found so far
items: Transmission rises steadily with the resonance and the mode width held.
The design is a gentle rise in corrugation toward the arms, a mild overshoot.
The post row does not move when freed: its optimum is separable and set analytically.
\textcolor{green!50!black}{About 6× the plain grating} at the operating point, still below the lab's TE overshoot.

frames.title: Next steps
items: Restart the inverse design with more free teeth.
Adapt the overshoot apodization model to TM and use it as the starting point.
A TE lane seeded from the overshoot profile, where the larger gains are.
